blocks.text: A briefing for Jason Myers and the interview group, prepared by Sandra Fuentes, with Jeffrey Patterson on research and James Grant on process. The engagement began {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}} and is scoped to run about three months. This briefing covers the opening phase of the work: what we have done, what the market has said back to us so far, and what we would ask of you before the slate is drawn.

items: The position specification is settled and signed off, and every approach we have made since has been made against it.
The company map is agreed, covering the sector itself and the two adjacent ones, with the reason each company is on it recorded.
Approaches are underway. These are conversations rather than applications; almost nobody we want is looking.
There is no slate yet, and there should not be. A slate drawn at this point would be a list of the people who answered first.

blocks.text: What the market is telling us

items: The role reads well to operators who have been through a growth stretch, and reads as a step sideways to sitting finance chiefs at much larger companies.
The board exposure written into the specification is the part that draws people in.
Two candidates asked early how decisions actually get made and who owns the annual plan. Expect that question in your interviews.
Compensation is not an obstacle so far, though we will know more once we are talking with people who would have to leave something behind.

blocks.text: How we are protecting the process

items: Candidates are described by their current role and never by name in anything that circulates, including these pages.
Jeffrey Patterson holds the target list and the reasoning behind each name, so that any candidate who reaches you can be defended.
James Grant holds the interview calendar. Windows are confirmed before a candidate is told anything about dates.
Nothing about this search is put in writing outside the engagement team and your interview group.

blocks.text: What we would ask of you

items: Two half-day windows held for the interview group, so that the slate review is not waiting on calendars once it is ready.
A view from Jason Myers on whether the board members meet finalists together or separately.
Feedback within a day of each meeting. Candidates read a long silence as a decision that has already been made.
